title: The Car That Wouldn't Move
hook: Bolt won't budge before the Big Garage Race — can Brian, Jasmine and Marcus find out why?
core_lesson: Engineers test one possible cause at a time — and listen to every teammate.
adult_safety_note: Children only handle toys, paper and cardboard. Auntie Ada (an adult) uses the tweezers and handles the battery-powered toy's switch tests.

learning_objectives.goal: Four wheels per car; three groups of four make 12 (4 + 4 + 4 = 12, 3 × 4 = 12).
Battery, motor, axle and wheels each do a different job.
Test one possible cause at a time instead of guessing.
Friction from a fluffy surface slows a rolling toy more than a smooth board.
Listening to Jasmine and Marcus leads to a better plan.
Toys and paper models only; an adult handles tools and batteries.

talk_together: What clue did Jasmine notice that Brian missed?
Find something at home that rolls. Does it roll farther on a rug or on a smooth floor?
Brian said sorry. Why do you think that helped the team?

complete.recall: Engineers test one thing at a time — and listen to everyone!
complete.question: Where at home could you run your own fair test with a toy car? (Ask a grown-up to help.)

season.title: The Mystery of the Missing Wheels

interactions.label: Spot the clue
interactions.prompt: Tap the part of Bolt that is stuck.
interactions.hint: Remember the push test: which wheels stayed still? Look closely there.
interactions.explain: A thread was wrapped around the back axle, so the back wheels couldn't turn. Finding the real cause beats guessing!

interactions.label: Choose a plan
interactions.prompt: Brian wants to test Bolt again. What is the best plan?

options.text: Brian does every job by himself.
Everyone gets a job that fits them.
Skip the test and just race.

interactions.hint: Think about what Jasmine and Marcus are good at. Who spotted the clues?
interactions.explain: Great leaders share the jobs. Jasmine draws the chart, Marcus counts, Brian sets the start line — and Auntie Ada checks safety.

interactions.label: Count the wheels
interactions.prompt: Three cars need four wheels each. How many wheels?
interactions.hint: Let's count together: one car has 4 wheels. Add 4 for each car.

interactions.label: Make a prediction
interactions.prompt: Where will Bolt roll farther: on the fluffy mat or the smooth board?
interactions.explain: Scientists make a prediction, then test it. Keep reading to find out what happens!

panels.visual: Brian grins at Bolt waiting on a taped start line.
panels.caption: Sunbeam Junction. Saturday morning in the Big Garage.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Ready, Bolt? Today we practise for the Big Garage Race!

panels.alt_text: Brian smiles and points at Bolt, a small orange toy car, waiting beside a taped start line in a sunny garage.

panels.visual: Jasmine draws a checkered finish flag at a small table.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: I'm drawing the finish flag. Checkers, like a real race!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine kneels at a low table, drawing a black-and-white checkered flag with a crayon.

panels.visual: Marcus lines up three toy cars in a row.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Car, car, car! Three cars!

panels.alt_text: Little Marcus points proudly at three toy cars — teal, purple and yellow — lined up on the floor.

panels.visual: Brian flips Bolt's switch on.
panels.caption: Bolt is a battery-powered toy. Its little motor turns the back wheels.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Switch on… three, two, one… GO!

panels.alt_text: Brian reaches toward Bolt and flips the small switch on its roof. A CLICK sound pops out.

panels.visual: Bolt shakes and hums, but its wheels stay still.
panels.caption: Bolt hums… but it doesn't move.
panels.alt_text: Close-up of Bolt shaking in place with a whirring sound. Its wheels are not moving.

panels.visual: Brian throws up his hands. Jasmine and Marcus watch.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Bolt won't go! And the race is in one week!

panels.alt_text: Brian throws both hands in the air, shocked. Jasmine and Marcus look on from the side. Bolt sits still.

panels.visual: Brian imagines a dead battery.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: The battery must be dead. We need a new one!

panels.alt_text: Brian frowns with his hand on his chin. A thought bubble shows a battery crossed out.

panels.visual: Jasmine raises her hand. Brian waves her off.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Wait! I heard a whirr. Doesn't that mean the battery works?

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: No time, Jasmine. I know cars!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine raises her hand with a question. Brian stands with his hand on his hip, not listening.

panels.visual: Marcus points at Bolt's wheel. Brian ignores him.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Wheel! Wheel!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Not now, Marcus.

panels.alt_text: Marcus hops and points at Bolt's back wheel. Brian looks away. Jasmine looks sad.

panels.visual: Auntie Ada walks in and waves.
panels.caption: Auntie Ada is an automotive engineer. She helps design real cars.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: What a busy garage! What's the problem, engineers?

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada, tall in navy overalls and an amber headwrap with goggles, waves as she walks into the garage. Brian turns to her.

panels.visual: Brian explains; Ada thinks.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Bolt is broken. The battery's dead, I'm sure!

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Maybe. How could we find out for sure?

panels.alt_text: Brian points at Bolt, looking upset. Auntie Ada kneels nearby with a thoughtful look.

panels.visual: Ada holds up a checklist of possible causes.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Engineers test one possible cause at a time.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada holds up a clipboard checklist with three pictures: a wheel, an axle rod and a battery. None are ticked yet.

fact.title: What is troubleshooting?
fact.text: Troubleshooting means finding what's wrong by checking possible causes one by one. If you change lots of things at once, you can't tell which one fixed it!

panels.visual: Close-up of Bolt with the back axle glowing.
panels.caption: New word: AXLE — the rod that joins two wheels so they turn together.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: See this rod? That's an axle. Bolt's motor spins the back axle.

panels.alt_text: A big close-up of Bolt. The rod joining the back wheels glows with a highlight circle.

panels.visual: Brian gets it; Ada traces the energy path.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: So the motor turns the axle, and the axle turns the wheels!

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Exactly. Battery, motor, axle, wheels.

panels.alt_text: Brian's face lights up with understanding. Auntie Ada smiles and nods. An energy path drawing floats between them: battery, motor, axle, wheels.

fact.title: Bolt's energy path (simplified toy)
fact.text: Battery → wires and switch → motor → axle → wheels. This is a simplified toy diagram. Real electric cars add power electronics and many more systems, and not every car works the same way.

panels.visual: Ada switches Bolt off for the first test.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: First test: switch OFF. Then gently push Bolt and watch the wheels.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: A push test!

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada switches Bolt off. The switch on its roof turns grey. Brian kneels, ready to help.

panels.visual: Brian gives Bolt a gentle push; it scrapes forward a little.
panels.caption: Test 1: switch off, gentle push.
panels.alt_text: Brian gently pushes Bolt. It scrapes forward only a tiny bit with a SCRRK sound.

panels.visual: Front wheel spins; back wheel stays still. A thin thread is visible near the back wheel.
panels.caption: The front wheels spin. The back wheels stay still.
panels.alt_text: Close-up of Bolt. The front wheel spins. The back wheel doesn't move. A thin red thread can be seen near the back wheel.

panels.visual: Brian is puzzled. Jasmine offers a magnifying glass.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Weird. Only the front wheels turn.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Can I look closer?

panels.alt_text: Brian scratches his head, puzzled. Jasmine holds up a magnifying glass.

panels.visual: Jasmine peers through the magnifying glass at Bolt.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Look closely! Can YOU spot what's wrong?

panels.alt_text: Jasmine kneels and peers through a magnifying glass at Bolt's back wheel.

panels.visual: Magnified: a thread tangled around the back axle.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Something is wrapped around the back axle!

panels.alt_text: Through the magnifying glass: a long red thread is tangled tightly around Bolt's back axle.

panels.visual: Marcus cheers; Brian realises he didn't listen.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Wheel! Me said wheel!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: You were both right… and I didn't listen.

panels.alt_text: Marcus jumps with his arms up. Brian looks down, embarrassed. Jasmine watches him.

panels.visual: Brian kneels to his siblings' level and apologises.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Jasmine, Marcus — I'm sorry. I should have listened to you.

panels.alt_text: Brian bends down to face Jasmine and Marcus and says sorry, one hand on his chest.

panels.visual: Jasmine and Marcus forgive Brian with a team hug.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: That's okay. We're a team.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: TEAM!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine and Marcus hug Brian. Everyone is smiling.

panels.visual: Ada smiles warmly.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Good engineers listen. Everyone notices different clues.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada smiles warmly with her hand over her heart.

panels.visual: Ada picks up tweezers; the children watch from a safe spot.
panels.caption: Bolt's switch is still off.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Tools are a grown-up job. You can be my detectives.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada holds a pair of tweezers. Brian and Jasmine watch from a step back.

panels.visual: Tweezers pull the tangled thread off the axle.
panels.caption: Auntie Ada gently pulls out a long, tangled thread.
panels.alt_text: Close-up: tweezers pull a long red thread off Bolt's back axle with a TUG.

panels.visual: Ada holds up the thread; Jasmine recognises her yarn.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Long string!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: That's from my yarn basket! Oops.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada holds up a long dangling red thread. Marcus stares. Jasmine covers her mouth, giggling — it's her yarn.

panels.visual: Brian thinks about how to lead the next test.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Let's test again. But what's the best plan?

panels.alt_text: Brian taps his chin, thinking. Jasmine and Marcus wait beside him.

panels.visual: Brian gives jobs to Jasmine and Marcus.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Jasmine, you draw our results chart. Marcus, you count the wheels!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: I'll make it colourful!

panels.alt_text: Brian gestures to Jasmine and Marcus. Jasmine holds up her crayons, excited.

panels.visual: Brian asks Ada to check safety.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: I'll set the start line. Auntie Ada, can you check safety?

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Happy to, team leader.

panels.alt_text: Brian looks up at Auntie Ada and asks for help. She gives a thumbs-up.

panels.visual: Marcus brings three toy cars for test day.
panels.caption: Marcus brings three more cars for test day.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Three cars! Count wheels!

panels.alt_text: Marcus stands proudly beside three toy cars — teal, purple and yellow.

panels.visual: Brian poses the wheel question.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Each car has four wheels. How many wheels must we check?

panels.alt_text: Brian points at the three toy cars. Jasmine thinks hard.

panels.visual: Marcus counts the wheels, which light up four at a time.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: One, two, three… TWELVE!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Twelve wheels. All spinning freely!

panels.alt_text: The three toy cars with all twelve wheels spinning. Marcus counts with his fingers; Brian gives a thumbs-up.

panels.visual: Ada supervises as Brian switches Bolt on.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Push test passed. Now a motor test, with me right here.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Switch… ON!

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada kneels beside Brian as he switches Bolt on. CLICK!

panels.visual: Bolt zooms across the floor.
panels.caption: It works!
panels.alt_text: Bolt zooms across the garage floor with speed lines behind it. VROOM!

panels.visual: Everyone cheers.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Bolt is back!

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Vroom vroom!

panels.alt_text: Brian, Jasmine and Marcus cheer with their arms in the air.

panels.visual: Bolt drives onto the fluffy mat and slows down.
panels.caption: But on the fluffy mat, Bolt slows right down.
panels.alt_text: Bolt drives onto a fluffy pink mat and slows to a crawl. A soft 'fwump' sound.

panels.visual: Brian worries; Jasmine points out the mat.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Uh-oh. Is Bolt broken again?

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: No! It's slower on the fluffy mat.

panels.alt_text: Brian looks worried. Jasmine points at the fluffy mat where Bolt crawls slowly.

panels.visual: Ada explains friction.
panels.caption: New word: FRICTION.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: That's friction — a rubbing force that slows things down.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada rubs her hands together to show friction, smiling.

fact.title: More about friction
fact.text: Fluffy or rough surfaces usually make more friction than smooth ones. Try rubbing your hands together — that warm feeling is friction! Real results also depend on the wheels, the toy and the push.

panels.visual: Brian proposes a race on two surfaces.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Let's race Bolt on the mat AND the smooth board!

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Good idea. Let's make it a fair test.

panels.alt_text: Brian points excitedly at a fluffy mat and a smooth wooden board on the floor. Auntie Ada nods.

panels.visual: Ada sets up a cardboard ramp.
panels.caption: New words: FAIR TEST. Bolt's switch stays off — the ramp gives the same start every time.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Same car, same ramp, same start. We change only the surface.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada places a small cardboard ramp at the start of the board, with Bolt switched off at the top.

fact.title: What makes a test fair?
fact.text: In a fair test you change only ONE thing (here, the surface) and keep everything else the same: the same car, the same ramp, the same starting spot, and no pushing.

panels.visual: Jasmine and Marcus make predictions.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: I predict… the smooth board!

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Mat! Mat!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine points to the smooth board. Marcus points to the fluffy mat. Each has a guess.

panels.visual: Brian lets go of Bolt at the top of the ramp, onto the mat.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Just let go. No pushing!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Ready… release!

panels.alt_text: Brian opens his hand at the top of the ramp, letting Bolt roll down toward the fluffy mat. Auntie Ada watches.

panels.visual: Bolt stops after three blocks on the mat; Marcus counts.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: One, two, three blocks!

panels.alt_text: Bolt has stopped on the fluffy mat beside the third counting block. Marcus counts the blocks.

panels.visual: Jasmine draws the first bar on her chart.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Mat: three blocks. I'll draw a short bar.

panels.alt_text: Jasmine holds up her chart. One short pink bar shows the mat result: three blocks.

panels.visual: Same ramp, now onto the smooth board.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Same ramp. Same spot. Let go!

panels.alt_text: Brian lets Bolt go from the same ramp, now facing the smooth wooden board. WHOOSH!

panels.visual: Bolt rolls seven blocks on the smooth board.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: …six, seven! SEVEN blocks!

panels.alt_text: Bolt rolls all the way to the seventh counting block on the smooth board. Marcus jumps with excitement.

panels.visual: Jasmine's finished chart compares both bars.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: Board: seven blocks. That's four more than the mat!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Less friction, farther roll!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine's chart shows a short pink bar for the mat (3 blocks) and a tall teal bar for the board (7 blocks). Brian grins.

panels.visual: Marcus lies on the mat pretending to be a car.
panels.caption: Marcus runs his own friction test.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Me a car! Vroom!

panels.alt_text: Marcus lies on his tummy on the fluffy mat with his arms out like a car, not moving at all.

panels.visual: Marcus gives up dramatically; everyone laughs.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Too much friction!

panels.alt_text: Marcus flops on the mat, declaring 'Too much friction!' Brian and Jasmine burst out laughing.

panels.visual: Ada laughs too.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Excellent data, Marcus!

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada laughs and gives Marcus a thumbs-up.

panels.visual: Race day: bunting, smooth board track, Jasmine's flag.
panels.caption: One week later: the Big Garage Race!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Axle checked. Wheels checked. Smooth track. Ready!

panels.alt_text: The garage is decorated with colourful bunting. Bolt waits at the start of a smooth board track. Jasmine holds her checkered flag at the finish.

panels.visual: Bolt zooms down the track.
panels.alt_text: Bolt zooms down the smooth track with speed lines. VROOOM!

panels.visual: Bolt crosses the finish; everyone cheers.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: It finished!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Because we did it together!

panels.alt_text: Bolt crosses the finish line. Brian, Jasmine, Marcus and Auntie Ada cheer together under the bunting.

panels.visual: Brian and Jasmine share what they learned.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Test one thing at a time.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: And look closely for clues!

panels.alt_text: Brian holds up one finger. Jasmine holds up her magnifying glass.

panels.visual: Marcus adds his lesson; Brian laughs.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: And listen to Marcus!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: And listen to everybody.

panels.alt_text: Marcus puts his hands on his hips proudly. Brian laughs and ruffles his hair.

panels.visual: Ada sums up; closing safety message.
panels.caption: Safe engineering: toys, paper, cardboard — and a grown-up helper.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: That's how engineers work. And grown-ups handle tools and batteries.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada smiles beside the pegboard of tools, which hangs high up out of children's reach.

panels.visual: That night, Marcus opens the spare-wheels box.
panels.caption: That night…
panels.alt_text: In the evening garage, Marcus opens a cardboard box marked for spare wheels.

panels.visual: The box is empty. Marcus gasps.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Uh-oh. Wheels… GONE!

panels.alt_text: Close-up: the spare-wheels box is completely empty. Marcus's eyes go wide.

panels.visual: Brian and Jasmine rush in, ready for a new mystery.
panels.caption: Next time: The Mystery of the Missing Wheels!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: A new mystery? Team — let's go!

panels.alt_text: Brian and Jasmine rush in with a torch-shaped magnifier, ready to solve the mystery with Marcus.
